To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

local administration of cytostatics can induce a long-lasting, antigen-specific state of enhanced cell-mediated immune reactivity, and that the effect is due to selective toxicity for suppressors cells and/or to a direct, stimulatory action on T effector cells.
local application of cytostatics to the site of sensitization enhances the immune response to the sensitizing antigen.

local chemotherapy can induce an enhanced state of T cell responsiveness, and that the mechanism of this enhancement involves selective toxicity for suppressive cells and selective sparing of effector cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of locally applied cytostatic drugs in mice.
the development of new immunopotentiating protocols based on a combination of cytostatic drugs with antigenic stimuli.
the development of an immunopotentiating protocol for cancer patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
local chemotherapy with CY-derivatives or VP-16 can be used to enhance the development of cell mediated immunity in mice.

local chemotherapy with Z 7557 or VP-16 is able to augment the T effector cell response by selectively destroying suppressor cells and by inducing the proliferation and activation of effector cells in the draining lymph nodes.
locally administered cytostatics, by selective toxicity for T suppressor cells, can enhance T helper cell functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
locally applied cytotoxic drugs can be used as immunopotentiating agents.
local chemotherapy can be used as an immunopotentiating tool to improve the efficiency of vaccination and tumor rejection.
locally applied cytotoxic drugs can enhance T cell responses to antigens in vivo by a combination of selective toxicity to T suppressor cells and a delayed onset of T effector cell toxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of local chemotherapy for enhancing cell-mediated responses may be of interest for the treatment of cancer patients.
local chemotherapy can induce long-lasting states of enhanced T cell reactivity, which may be of interest for the treatment of tumors and chronic infections.
locally administered cytostatics can induce an enhanced state of DTH responsiveness.
